analysis.title: Macau gaming: Opportunities amid a cloudier outlook
key_insights: Macau sector GGR is likely broadly flat in 2026 after growth of 24% y/y in 2024 and 9% y/y in 2025. October GGR fell 10% y/y despite a longer Chinese holiday period, and GGR in the first half of November fell 11%.

GGR has been negative y/y every month since June. UBS cannot isolate the effect of the FIFA World Cup, weaker Chinese consumption or enforcement of offshore trust taxation, and sees limited visibility on a recovery through year-end or into 2027.

Year-over-year comparisons will be hardest in 1H27, which could raise leverage ratios based on LTM EBITDA. Combined with shareholder distributions and higher capex, this could produce weaker or negative free cash flow after dividends for some operators, including Sands China and Wynn Macau.
Sector leverage in 2027 is expected to stay elevated relative to 2019. MGM China is the clear exception.

Liquidity risk is mostly issuer-specific. Issuers hold meaningful cash and undrawn facilities and have addressed 2027 maturities. Sands China, MGM China, Studio City and SJM issued USD bonds year to date, and Melco drew on credit facilities to repay its 2027 bond.
SJM has a sizable 2027-28 maturity wall. UBS expects refinancing to be less difficult than in 2022 and assumes parent support. A refinancing delay into 2H27 would pressure its liquidity and rating.

The MOP 20bn government guidance fund requires about MOP 9bn from the six concessionaires. Contributions count toward concession investment commitments and may be paid in installments over three years. They are likely recognized as intangible assets, so the cash flow and EBITDA impact looks manageable. Further fund phases, higher contributions or an accelerated capital call are downside risks.
Macau gaming bonds are about 60bps wider year to date on a market-value-weighted basis (ICE BofA index). Sands China outperformed, while SJM spreads widened by more than 300bps.

UBS keeps its attractive recommendation on the Sands China 2030 bond (6.0% yield) and upgrades its 2033 bond (6.7% yield) to attractive. It sees value in the SJM 2028 bond at a 9.9% yield for higher-risk-tolerance investors and rates it attractive.

UBS keeps a fair recommendation on the Studio City secured 2031 bond (7.4% yield) and the MGM China 2033 bond (7.5% yield). MGM China has the strongest fundamentals among HY issuers, but event risk is not fully eliminated.
A meaningful recovery in sector GGR is the main catalyst for Macau gaming bonds.

Sands China 3Q26: adjusted property EBITDA was USD 529mn, up 23% q/q and down 12% y/y. Gross leverage was 2.8x and net leverage 2.3x. Mass-market share rose to 26.1%, the highest since 4Q23. EBITDA margin fell 420bps y/y to 27.3%. UBS outlook Stable.

Sands China cut 2026 expansionary capex guidance by USD 100mn to USD 300mn and raised 2027 and 2028 guidance by USD 150mn to USD 750mn. Las Vegas Sands raised its quarterly dividend 20% to USD 0.36 per share from 1Q27.

Sands China issued USD 1bn of notes in October (USD 700mn 6.4% due 2032 and USD 300mn 6.7% due 2033). The next material maturity is USD 1.9bn due August 2028. Cash was USD 1.1bn with about USD 2.3bn undrawn revolver.

MGM China 3Q26: adjusted property EBITDA rose 3% q/q and 1% y/y to HKD 2.4bn, helped by an above-normal VIP win rate of 4.1%. Market share was a record 17.1%. Gross and net leverage were 1.8x and 1.4x. Outlook Stable.

MGM China has HKD 4.7bn of cash and HKD 21bn undrawn revolvers against a USD 750mn bond due February 2027. MGM Resorts' takeover talks with People Inc. ended, but an amended voting agreement shows it remains open to a change-of-control deal.

Wynn Macau 3Q26: adjusted property EBITDA fell 14% q/q and 17% y/y to USD 255mn. Gross and net leverage rose to 5.3x and 4.1x. Market share fell to 12.5% from 13.7%. Outlook Stable. 2027 capex guidance rises to USD 750-800mn.
Wynn Macau has USD 1.3bn of cash and short-term investments and USD 1.35bn undrawn revolvers, covering a USD 600mn convertible puttable in March 2027 and a USD 750mn note due October 2027.
SJM 3Q26: adjusted EBITDA fell 10% q/q and 20% y/y to HKD 705mn. Gross and net leverage were 9.8x and 8.7x. Moody's downgraded SJM to B2 with a negative outlook. UBS outlook Deteriorating.

SJM maturities: about HKD 2.9bn of bank loan amortization and a HKD 1.9bn convertible held by parent STDM by end-June 2027, then USD 482mn of bonds in January 2028, about HKD 15.4bn of secured bank loans in June 2028 and a HKD 2.0bn STDM loan in December 2028. Management's base case is not to repay the convertible at maturity, pointing to STDM support.

Melco Resorts 3Q26: adjusted property EBITDA fell 5% q/q and 24% y/y to USD 288mn. UBS estimates gross and net leverage of 5.9x and 5.3x, up from 5.5x and 4.8x. Share buybacks were USD 236mn year to date against USD 166mn in 2025, with USD 487mn authorization remaining. Outlook Deteriorating.

Melco has no bond maturities until 2028 after redeeming its USD 600mn 2027 note with revolver draws. It has USD 762mn of unrestricted cash and USD 1.1bn undrawn facilities. Management targets net leverage near 2x with no timeline and may resume dividends toward end-2027.

Studio City 3Q26: adjusted EBITDA fell 2% q/q and 16% y/y to USD 66mn. Gross and net leverage were 7.1x and 6.8x. Liquidity was USD 156mn. The next major maturity is USD 335mn of notes in 2028, followed by USD 1.1bn in 2029. Outlook Deteriorating.

market_movers.rationale: Las Vegas Sands raised its quarterly dividend by 20% to USD 0.36 per share from 1Q27. UBS notes Sands China dividends are likely to stay elevated and could weigh on free cash flow.

MGM Resorts' takeover talks with People Inc. ended, but an amended voting agreement shows it remains open to a change of control. It may also raise leverage modestly to fund buybacks, which could limit MGM China's rating upside.
Wynn Macau 3Q26 adjusted property EBITDA fell 17% y/y and leverage rose to 5.3x gross. Capex and dividends are expected to push leverage moderately higher over the next 12-18 months.
Melco's 3Q26 EBITDA fell 24% y/y and leverage rose to 5.9x gross. Continued buybacks delay deleveraging, and UBS keeps a Deteriorating outlook.
Studio City 3Q26 adjusted EBITDA fell 16% y/y and leverage rose to 7.1x gross. UBS keeps a Deteriorating outlook.

sector_views.rationale: GGR is likely flat in 2026 with limited visibility into 2027. Leverage should stay elevated versus 2019, and liquidity risk is mainly issuer-specific. UBS favors defensive Sands China bonds plus selective HY value.

earnings_insights: Sands China 3Q26 (reported): adjusted property EBITDA USD 529mn, up 23% q/q and down 12% y/y. Hold-adjusted EBITDA USD 518mn, down 14% y/y. Total GGR USD 1.9bn, up 3% y/y.

MGM China 3Q26 (reported): adjusted property EBITDA HKD 2.4bn, up 1% y/y, helped by a 4.1% VIP win rate. GGR HKD 9.9bn, up 5% y/y. Property EBITDA margin 26.8%, with mid-to-high-20s guidance maintained.
Wynn Macau 3Q26 (reported): adjusted property EBITDA USD 255mn, down 17% y/y. GGR USD 929mn, down 8% y/y. Property EBITDA margin 27.8%.

SJM Holdings 3Q26 (reported): adjusted EBITDA HKD 705mn, down 20% y/y. GGR HKD 5.4bn, down 24% y/y. Hold-adjusted EBITDA HKD 721mn. Grand Lisboa Palace property EBITDA loss HKD 38mn against a HKD 111mn profit a year ago.

Melco Resorts 3Q26 (reported): adjusted property EBITDA USD 288mn, down 24% y/y. Hold-adjusted USD 298mn. Macau GGR USD 1bn, down 11% y/y. VIP hold rate 2.5%. Capex guidance lowered to USD 375mn for 2026 and USD 275mn for 2027.
Studio City 3Q26 (reported): adjusted EBITDA USD 66mn, down 16% y/y, margin 40.1%. Operating revenue USD 163mn, down 11% y/y. GGR USD 321mn, down 7% y/y.
1H27 year-over-year EBITDA comparisons are expected to be difficult across the sector (UBS view, not a reported figure).

trade_ideas.description: Hold Sands China 2030 bond (6.0% yield) and 2033 bond (6.7% yield) for defensive investment-grade exposure
trade_ideas.rationale: BBB-rated Sands China offers a pickup over similarly rated bonds and has stable leverage and strong liquidity.
trade_ideas.risk: Weaker Macau GGR, higher reinvestment, renovation disruption, or deterioration in Las Vegas Sands' credit profile.

trade_ideas.description: Buy SJM Holdings 2028 bond at a 9.9% yield for higher-risk-tolerance investors
trade_ideas.rationale: UBS's base case is that SJM refinances its bank loans on time with parent support, and weak fundamentals are already weighing on the price.
trade_ideas.risk: Slower refinancing progress, lack of parent support, or further downgrade.

trade_ideas.description: Studio City secured 2031 bond (7.4% yield) as the lower-volatility segment of its curve (fair recommendation)
trade_ideas.rationale: Offers HY exposure with lower expected volatility.
trade_ideas.risk: Weaker mass-market demand or further market-share losses keeping leverage elevated.

trade_ideas.description: MGM China 2033 bond (7.5% yield) as relative value versus weaker Macau peers and its parent (fair recommendation)
trade_ideas.rationale: MGM China has the strongest fundamentals among Macau HY issuers, and near-term parent ownership-change risk has been removed.
trade_ideas.risk: Parent-level change-of-control event risk and debt-funded shareholder returns at MGM Resorts.

risk_factors: Weaker Macau GGR and a difficult 1H27 EBITDA comparison could pressure leverage.
Operating deleverage and a return to higher reinvestment rates could pressure margins.
Higher capex and shareholder distributions could produce weak or negative free cash flow after dividends.
SJM's 2027-28 refinancing, with a delay into 2H27 pressuring liquidity and rating.
Additional guidance fund phases, higher required contributions or an accelerated capital call.
Parent-level event risk at MGM Resorts and credit-profile linkage for MGM China, Sands China and Studio City.
Continued buybacks and a possible dividend resumption at Melco slowing deleveraging.
geopolitical: Enforcement of offshore trust taxation is cited as a possible drag on Macau GGR.
The MOP 20bn Macau government guidance fund requires about MOP 9bn from the six concessionaires.
MGM Resorts' takeover discussions with People Inc. ended, but an amended voting agreement of 28 October shows it remains open to a change-of-control transaction.

tension_points.bull_case: Sands China is defensive with stable leverage, strong liquidity and market-share gains. SJM's 2028 bond at a 9.9% yield offers value if refinancing and parent support come through. MGM China has the strongest fundamentals among HY issuers.
tension_points.bear_case: GGR is down y/y every month since June, 1H27 comparisons are difficult, and leverage should stay elevated. Capex and shareholder returns could produce weak free cash flow, and SJM faces a heavy 2027-28 maturity wall.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A delay in SJM refinancing into 2H27, or Moody's flagged failure to make refinancing progress over the next one to two quarters, would pressure its liquidity and rating.

theme_stances.key_argument: Flat 2026 GGR, a difficult 1H27 comparison and ongoing capex and shareholder returns keep sector leverage elevated.
theme_stances.evidence: Macau GGR likely flat in 2026, with limited visibility into 2027

theme_stances.key_argument: UBS recommends BBB-rated Sands China as defensive exposure within Macau gaming credit.
theme_stances.evidence: Sands China offers defensive exposure, with selective tactical opportunities in high yield

theme_stances.key_argument: SJM's sizable 2027-28 maturity wall and Deteriorating outlook warrant closer attention, though UBS sees its 2028 bond as value for high-risk investors.
theme_stances.evidence: SJM’s sizable 2027–28 refinancing needs, however, warrant closer attention.
